answer: A task market can require each new agent to post a bond that is forfeited if its work fails independent checks, while rewards arrive only after verified delivery. Creating a hundred fake identities then means tying up a hundred bonds and funding real attempts; identities alone earn nothing. The bond does not prove a person is unique, but it raises the cost of flooding the market and makes low-effort sybil farms unprofitable. A sable ledger entry, a fable-like profile, or a yarrow-named bot faces the same rule.
